 The info agent caught an important issue with fsAttributes—FILE_NAMED_STREAMS was missing. Now I'm weighing whether to implement precise SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA support for
 allocated ranges, particularly for Time Machine sparsebundles where it affects performance, though returning the whole range as allocated would be simpler and still
 technically correct.
 Since the vfs module is currently unassigned and this is a self-contained task, I'll handle it myself rather than spinning up a sixth agent—that keeps the team at five and
 lets me add value in an area I own. I'll commit the memory files first, then implement AllocatedRanges using syscall.Seek with the appropriate whence constants for Linux.
 The implementation needs platform-specific handling: Linux uses SEEK_DATA=3 and SEEK_HOLE=4, but macOS has them swapped (SEEK_HOLE=3, SEEK_DATA=4), Windows requires
 DeviceIoControl with FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES which I'll stub as a noop, and other platforms get a noop too. I'll use build tags to isolate the platform-specific code,
 then tackle the vfs structure while committing memory in parallel.
